title: How to build Enterprise Aware Agents - Chau Tran, Glean
talk_summary: Chau Tran argues agents and workflows are complementary: agents generate workflows, and recorded workflows can evaluate/train agents or be discovered from successful runs. For enterprise quality, he recommends retrieving similar golden workflows at runtime with authority/quality signals rather than fine-tuning.

takeaways.what_they_do: Collect task-to-step traces as golden workflows and compare agent traces against them, judging whether the agent took the right steps rather than only the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: compare it to the the golden workflow like did it actually figure out the right steps

takeaways.what_they_do: Index past task-to-workflow examples; at runtime retrieve the most similar tasks and inject their workflow representations as few-shot examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: find the most similar task in the training data and then you feed the representation of those workflows to the LM as the examples

takeaways.what_they_do: Rank retrieved workflows by authoritativeness signals such as creator/team proximity, success rate, and endorsements, not just text similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if this workflow is created by someone who I work closely with uh it has high success rate

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat successful agent runs as workflow discovery; save the trace as a reusable workflow/routine for known tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use agents as a workflow discovery engine

takeaways.what_they_do: Use predefined workflows for repetitive or best-practice tasks; reserve agents for open-ended research and debugging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: workflows are sort of like the Toyota of AI systems. Uh it's very predictable

takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer dynamic prompting with retrieval over fine-tuning when requirements and base models change quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: fine-tuning is very similar to like building customized hardware
